clue.text: Distortion according to interpretation

parts.note: per means according to, as in 'per the rules'
a version is one person's interpretation or account

explanation.surface: A critic complains that a reading of a text twists it, depending on how you interpret it.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisting of the truth or of meaning is a perversion of it, a synonym of distortion.

clue.text: Get better vehicle

definitions.meaning: to recover or improve, as trade or health picks up

explanation.surface: An advert urging you to upgrade your car.
explanation.definitionFit: Improving is picking up, and a light truck with an open back is a pickup.

clue.text: Distant unfinished roadside building about to start

indicators.note: says the word for about comes at the beginning, before the building

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: the last letter of the building's name is left off

parts.note: a motel is a roadside hotel for motorists

explanation.surface: A half-built motel on a lonely highway is just about to open.
explanation.definitionFit: Something far away or isolated is remote, a plain synonym of distant.

clue.text: Raising the spirits of excited Thai relaxing

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: An agitated Thai person unwinding finds it uplifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' shuffles the letters of THAI RELAXING; 'of' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exhilarating is thrilling and cheering, so it lifts one's mood.

clue.text: Place in bedsit establishment

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words bedsit establishment, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Finding a spot in a block of bedsits, the cheap single-room flats Britons rent.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsit is a British one-room rented flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A location or position is a site, a plain synonym of place.

clue.text: Too much of article included in open work

indicators.note: the article is placed inside the word for open

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
the is the definite article
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A critic finds an open-air artwork overloaded with features.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the top is an idiom for excessive or exaggerated, more than is called for.

clue.text: Go, having emptied salt — salt!

indicators.note: the word salt has its middle removed, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, and AB (able seaman) is a sailor too

explanation.surface: A cook who has used up the salt cries out for more.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the second 'salt' as a different sense: an old sailor, crossword AB.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go is to have a stab, an idiom for making an attempt.

clue.text: To be one, this administrator must have two others

definitions.text: To be one, this administrator must have two others

parts.words: To be one, this administrator must have two others
parts.note: an official who is one of a governing group of three in ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A riddle about an official who needs two colleagues to hold office at all.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome power was sometimes shared by three magistrates, each one a member of a triumvirate.

clue.text: Teasing good for youth, presumably

definitions.meaning: read as a phrase: something good for the young is presumably ..., split as three words

explanation.surface: A view that being ribbed does young people good.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part is cryptic: what suits youth would be 'bad in age', which run together spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-hearted banter and joking exchanges are called badinage, from French.

clue.text: Seductive invitation to approach

explanation.surface: A flirtatious look that beckons someone over.
explanation.definitionFit: A come-hither look is alluring; literally the phrase is an old way of beckoning someone closer.

clue.text: Empty rhetoric, that's a blow

definitions.meaning: hot air, talk with no substance
moving air is a blow of the breeze

explanation.surface: A disappointed listener finds a speech hollow and says so.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk is dismissed as hot air, and moving air blowing about is the same word.

clue.text: Breach in border intended to be announced

parts.note: a fringe is an edge or border

indicators.note: spoken out, so the word for intended is entered by how it sounds

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A frontier violation that was planned to be publicly declared.
explanation.definitionFit: A violation of a rule or right is an infringement, a synonym of breach.

clue.text: Had not revealed such wealth

definitions.meaning: riches too great to count, a stock phrase

explanation.surface: Someone kept their fortune secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret never told is left unspoken, and vast riches are described as untold wealth.

clue.text: He might fall for actor

parts.note: a performer who takes the dangerous tumbles in place of a film star; 'fall for' looks like falling in love

explanation.surface: Someone might fall in love with a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall for' suggests being smitten; here it means taking a fall on an actor's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunt double performs risky falls and crashes in place of the star.

clue.text: Yours truly playing clarinet in commercial

parts.note: a setter's way of saying me

indicators.note: the letters of clarinet are played about with and rearranged

explanation.surface: The writer plays clarinet in a TV advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial' looks like a TV advert; here it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile is an adjective for trade and merchants, matching commercial.

clue.text: Losing water to make ice first, it's a way of preservation

indicators.note: places the word for making ice before the word for losing water

parts.note: to freeze water is to make ice
drying is losing moisture

explanation.surface: A food scientist describes a preserving process: chill, then dehydrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Freeze-drying preserves food or samples by freezing and then removing the ice under vacuum.

clue.text: Removal of European, the first person in France to get fresh tonic

parts.note: je is French for I, the first-person pronoun

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new arrangement of the letters of tonic

explanation.surface: A European guest is thrown out, and the first French customer gets a new tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing out or expelling is ejection, a synonym of removal.

clue.text: Instrumentalist going round station trapping serpent

indicators.note: the musician's name surrounds the station, holding it within
repeats the idea: the musician's name traps the station inside it

parts.note: a piper plays the bagpipes
ITV is a British commercial television station

explanation.surface: A street musician busking around a railway station catches a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' suggests a railway, but it is a British television channel; 'going round' and 'trapping' both signal the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Pit vipers are venomous snakes, such as rattlesnakes, with heat-sensing pits.

clue.text: Butcher's bill that's used by couples?

definitions.meaning: a bill for a joint of meat
a bank arrangement shared by two partners

explanation.surface: A wry remark that couples split the meat bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank account held by two people together is a joint account; jokingly, it is a bill for a joint of meat.

clue.text: Tex moving round posh party in formal wear

indicators.note: the rearranged name goes round the letter for posh
the letters of Tex are moved about

parts.note: U means upper-class in British usage
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A cowboy called Tex is moving around a smart party in his evening suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges TEX to TXE, and 'round' puts it around U.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuxedo is a dinner jacket, standard formal evening wear for men.

clue.text: Take out ad in support of peacekeepers

indicators.note: in a down answer the word below supports the one above, so the ad goes under the peacekeepers

parts.note: UN peacekeeping forces of the United Nations
a plug is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: An advertisement backing United Nations peace forces is pulled.
explanation.definitionFit: To unplug a device is to pull out its plug, taking it out of the socket.

clue.text: Contract to restore a convent

indicators.note: restoring puts the letters of a convent into a new working order

explanation.surface: A building contract has been signed to repair an old nunnery.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal agreement or binding promise, a synonym of contract.

clue.text: Endless quest organised at home for sparkly thing

indicators.note: the remaining letters are organised into a new order
the word quest loses its final letter

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A search conducted from home for a glittery item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' leaves QUES; 'organised' turns that into SEQU.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequin is a small shiny disc sewn onto clothes to make them glitter.

clue.text: No end of room for horses

indicators.note: the room's last letter is dropped

parts.note: a study is a room for working

explanation.surface: There's endless space for horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like 'plenty of', but it means cutting off the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a group of horses kept for breeding.

clue.text: One leading 1000 very good warriors

indicators.note: the letter for one comes before the rest

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
pi is short for pious, crossword shorthand for very good

explanation.surface: A single commander at the head of a thousand fine fighters.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment or band of armed men.

clue.text: Tiny foolish person stopped short, a Dickensian

parts.note: little means tiny

indicators.note: the word for a fool is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a nelly is a silly person, British slang

explanation.surface: A small idiot stops abruptly.
explanation.walkthrough: A NELLY is British slang for a silly or feeble person.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Nell is the heroine of Dickens's novel The Old Curiosity Shop.

clue.text: Lady's incomplete pattern

indicators.note: the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Norma is a woman's name; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A woman's dress pattern is unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a standard or usual model, a synonym of pattern.

clue.text: Powerful teacher first is obstinate

indicators.note: places the word for teacher before the word for powerful

parts.note: the head teacher of a school
strong means powerful

explanation.surface: A forceful headmistress who won't back down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wilful who refuses to be guided is headstrong, a synonym of obstinate.
